about: Radio and intercom for chapter 7: the lift-off from Taurus-Littrow to lunar orbit. Time lines follow the computer's ascent (liftoff-space.js: lift-off at GET 185:21:37, cut-off about 440 s later); ignition, the pitch-over and the cut-off are cued by what happens. t = GET (seconds from liftoff). Original lines in the style of the Apollo air-to-ground; not quotes.

lines.text: Challenger, Houston. You are go for lift-off. We are watching you on the rover's camera.
Ten seconds. Abort stage. Engine arm, ascent.
Ignition! We're on our way, Houston!
Challenger, Houston. A beautiful lift-off. Thrust looks good.
One minute. Guidance looks good. She's steady as a rock.
Challenger, Houston. Two minutes, and you are go.
Three minutes. Fifteen hundred feet a second, and the Moon just sliding by down there.
Challenger, Houston. Four minutes. You are go, right down the track.
Five and a half minutes. Thirty-six hundred feet a second.
Challenger, Houston. Standing by for cut-off.
Coming up on cut-off. Five hundred to go.
Challenger, Houston. We copy shutdown. You are in a nine by forty-eight mile orbit, and America is waiting for you up ahead.
Goodbye, Taurus-Littrow. Now let's go and find America.
